ground_truth.unit: SD of PISA math score per SD of national patience
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("National Preferences and Student Achievement across Countries: The Intertwined Roles of Patience and Risk-taking"), column (3), row Patience.  Student-level least squares regression of the PISA math test score (original PISA scores divided by 100, so a unit is one standard deviation), pooled over all PISA waves 2000-2018, on the country's Global Preference Survey patience and risk-taking entered together.  Each preference is z-standardised in the analytical sample and collapsed to the country level. Controls: student gender, age and migration status, imputation dummies, and test-wave fixed effects.  Weighted by students' sampling probabilities within countries, giving equal weight to each country.  Sample: all students in the 49 PISA countries with GPS data.  Robust standard errors clustered at the country level.

ground_truth.context: Table 1, column (3), row Risk-taking.  Same regression as table1_col3_patience (patience and risk-taking entered together).

ground_truth.unit: SD of PISA math score per SD of country-of-origin patience
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Patience, Risk-taking, and Student Achievement: Migrant Analysis"), column (3), row Patience (country-of-origin). Least squares regression of the PISA math score (divided by 100), PISA waves 2003-2018, on the GPS patience and risk-taking of the student's country of origin, entered together.  Sample: migrant students, both of whose parents were born outside the country where the student attends school, with an identified origin country that has GPS data.  First-generation migrants are assigned their country of birth, second-generation migrants their father's country of origin.  The sample spans 58 countries of origin and 48 residence countries.  Includes the 180 residence- country-by-wave fixed effects.  Controls: student gender, age, a dummy for an OECD country of origin, and imputation dummies. Robust standard errors clustered at the country-of-origin level.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Table 1 (pisa_full_gps_final.dta, 2.47 GB) cannot be read in full through the read-only mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (raw I/O roughly 5-15 MB/s; fread select= on the 2.8 GB CSV and haven col_select on the .dta both timed out). The final script parses the Stata 118 file directly, reading only the 14 needed columns from evenly spread blocks of 3000 consecutive rows (van der Corput order) until a 225 s deadline: 1,965,000 of 1,992,276 rows (98.6%), all 49 countries. Table 1 coefficients are therefore estimated on that subsample.
table1_col3_observations is the .dta header row count (1,992,276), reported because no row read has a missing regression variable; it is not the N of the subsample regression (1,965,000).

Table 1 standard errors are clustered on the country-level (patience, risk-taking) pair (49 distinct values) instead of the country string, which is a Stata strL that the direct parser does not decode. Coefficients are unaffected.

Table 2 uses the full migrant file (pisa_full_gps_final_imcoo.dta read with haven col_select) with no deviation: reg pv1math prefs female age imfemale image coo_oecd i.countrywave, cluster(coo) as feols(... | countrywave, cluster=~coo, fixef.rm='none'); image is constant (0) in this sample and drops for collinearity, as in Stata.
deviations_stdout: Table 1 estimated on 1965000 of 1992276 student rows (98.6%): the 2.47 GB pisa_full_gps_final.dta cannot be read through the mount within the 300 s sandbox limit, so the script parses the Stata file directly and reads only the needed columns from 655 evenly spread blocks of 3000 consecutive rows until a time deadline.

Table 1 standard errors are clustered on the country-level (patience, risk-taking) pair (49 distinct values) because the country variable is a Stata strL that the direct parser does not decode; coefficients are unaffected.
table1_col3_observations is the row count in the .dta header (N), reported because none of the rows read has a missing regression variable; the regression itself used only the subsample.
cell.notes: Seeded mode, following 3_analysis_crosscountry.do (Table 1: reg pv1math prefs female age migra1 migra2 image imfemale immigra1 i.wave [pw=wgtc], cluster(country); natives: migra0==1 without migration controls) and 3_analysis_migrants.do (Table 2). Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (no RESULT lines): 1 and 2 timed out reading the big file; 3 measured raw I/O and the .dta header. Attempt 4 (claim): 43% row subsample, and the strL bug gave a wrong cluster id; fixed cluster id and raised the read deadline. One run with deadline 262 s (02:07) hung during a Docker Desktop daemon wedge (container still up hours later) and a second launch never started a container; per the coordinator these are not attempts and are excluded (scratch copy kept outside the run dir). After the restart the deadline was set to 225 s. Attempt 5 (claim): 79.5% subsample in 12000-row blocks covered only 48 countries, so risk-taking was off; changed to 3000-row blocks. Final: 98.6% of rows, 49 countries; Table 2 reproduces exactly, Table 1 within about 0.01 of the claims except col1 patience 0.921 vs 0.917 and col2 risk -0.477 vs -0.482.
